Bottom line: We hosted Wanchen's retail-business CFO and capital market head at our event and left the meetings with enhanced confidence on clear growth visibility for 2026 and a compelling mid-to-long-term trajectory underpinned by the strategic focus on building a healthy franchising ecosystem, high-quality store expansion, and continued model/product innovation to deliver consumer value, amid rational competition in the industry. Key highlights: 1) 2026 outlook of robust store openings and improving single-store GMV trends: Company has already completed more store openings in 1H26 than the total openings in 2025 (4.1k/4.7k net/gross openings), with the pace dynamically balanced with healthy store UE (still within 2-year payback period). Mgmt shared that avg. per-store GMV achieved positive growth in 1H26 and tracking mgmt's full-year guidance of c.Rmb390k average monthly GMV (matching the 2H25 level) despite unfavorable weather and weak consumption sentiment, while SSSG trend is even better (given no new store dilution). Mgmt also expect new stores opened in 1H26 to ramp up in 2H26 on productivity. Moving forward, the company will continue prioritizing store health and balance store open pace vs. health per-store GMV performance (though not necessarily to accelerate store opening vs. 1H26); 2) SSSG resilience supported by operational refinement: Mgmt expressed strong confidence in SSSG resilience despite rapid scaling, supported by continued disciplined site selection, more curated category expansion, and sharper store operations amid rational pricing competition. New category has amounted to c. \(5\%\) of total GMV (c.3% from cold-chain products). Additionally, the company is prudently testing new formats (CVS and full-category discounters) to unlock new growth levers. 3) Profitability enhancement with GPM expansion and opex leverage: Mgmt maintained its full-year retail-business NPM (including MI) target at a slight expansion vs. c.5% in FY25, with opex ratio to continue refining YoY in FY26 on GPM expansion and op leverage (ie. logistics efficiency optimization on larger store network). Mgmt also see long-term GPM expansion headroom remains intact, driven by deepening scale efficiencies and procurement optimization. 4) Rational competitive landscape with disciplined subsidies: Mgmt emphasized that store-opening locations in 1H26 remains differentiated vs. competitors with \(70\%\) of openings concentrated in its stronghold markets (Yangtze River Delta/Shanhe Four Provinces). both industry leaders remain rational and disciplined over store-open subsidies, with special subsidies only approved for special location/regions and total subsidies level subdued yoy in 1H26. 5) Mgmt believes L-T expansion runway remains intact, supported by: i) meaningful share-gain potential versus traditional channels; ii) The company will maintain its focus on stronghold markets, noting runway for further penetration in certain prefecture-level cities; iii) enhancing franchise confidence signaled by existing franchisees contributing a high proportion of new openings (opening 2nd/3rd stores). The stock is trading at 14x/12x 2026/27E P/E vs. GSE of \(36\% /84\%\) sales/NP growth in 2026E. Reiterate Buy.

Key Takeaways
Mgmt decoded the growth path ahead in details:
Per-Store GMV drivers:

Category expansion: new categories now account for c.5% of total GMV, with chilled/frozen food at c.3% and others (IP, daily essentials, etc.) at c.2%, which is expected to prudently grow with the mix.

☐ Private Label (PL) scaling: PL SKU count grew from 30+ in FY25 to more than double in 2026, aiming for full-category coverage by year-end (expanding from a beverage-centric portfolio now). At this stage, mgmt positions PL to deliver better customer value and product differentiation to drive traffic/sales rather than seeking GPM accretion.

☐ Sharper operational tracking: Mgmt shared that store expansion metrics are monitored closely and rigorously internally, focusing on per-store GMV (monthly/daily sales) and payback periods. Rent-to-sales ratios are strictly controlled by the company as well (through ie. three-party negotiation).

□ Membership operations: mgmt shared that registered members grew from 190mn in end-2026 to 200mn+ with faster growth vs. store expansion. Active members' purchase frequency remained stable at 3 times/month, with a stable monthly contribution of c.Rmb90 per member, while active members numbers also increased vs. end-2025.
■ New store format expansion testing: Wanchen is actively exploring new formats to drive long-term differentiation:

☐ Discounter supermarket: An iterative community discount format where ambient snacks and beverages contribute 90% of GMV, while other categories (chilled/frozen, IP, daily essentials) make up 10% in stores carrying these SKUs.
Full-category hard discounter (Huishengjia / 惠省嘉): ~10 stores opened in Guangdong since early 2026, currently testing product assortments and locations with PL focus.
☐ Convenience Store format: Currently, only one pilot store is operating in Changsha, but mgmt is testing the model of which the expansion runway remains vast (c.320k CVS stores in China).

☐ Fresh Snacks: Mgmt is monitoring this high-growth niche-category store format in the industry while remain cautious about the scalability due to high cold chain costs/spoilage ratio/primary location requirement. Meanwhile, the company is testing cold-chain products.

Logistics and fulfillment efficiency: The company is investing in more warehouses to support faster replenishment requirement as outlet network expands. Despite these new investments, mgmt expects the overall logistics expense ratio to decline yoy driven by improved fulfillment efficiency.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - Fujian Wanchen Good

Valuation: Our 12m TP is Rmb319, based on a target 2027E P/E at 21.5x discounted back to end-2026E at an \(8.2\%\) COE. The target P/E is at a HSD% valuation discount to Busy Ming, as we reference the average gap of DLTR's NTM P/E vs. DG's in the past two years, factoring in the relatively slower network scaling momentum and less favorable UE (lower per-store GMV but profits driven by high mix of smaller brands/white labels).
Key risks: 1) intensifying market competition and price sustainability; 2) franchise model risk and scaling complexity; 3) M&A risks; 4) supply chain, food safety and logistics.

GS Factor Profile

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.
M&A Rank

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
